issues.legal_issue: A later suit for an omitted relief is barred when it arises from the same cause of action as an earlier suit, the plaintiff was entitled to claim multiple reliefs on that cause, and leave to omit the relief was not obtained.
material_facts: The plaintiff first sued for an injunction based on agreements to sell the properties and omitted to seek specific performance, although the first-suit pleadings alleged conduct showing that the defendant intended to frustrate the agreements.
The plaintiff asked for leave to reserve the specific-performance claim, but the court did not grant leave.
The plaintiff later brought suits for specific performance based on the same agreements and the same events pleaded in the earlier suits.
issues.conclusion: The later specific-performance suits were barred, and the plaints were struck off.
issues.legal_principle: Order II Rules 2(2) and 2(3) of the Code of Civil Procedure address, respectively, omission of part of a claim and omission of one of several reliefs. Under Gurbux Singh v. Bhooralal, the party invoking the bar must establish that the suits rest on the same cause of action, that more than one relief was available on that cause, and that the later relief was omitted without leave. The Court also relied on Deva Ram v. Ishwar Chand and M/s Bengal Waterproof Ltd. v. M/s Bombay Waterproof Manufacturing Co. The identity of a cause of action turns on the material facts entitling a plaintiff to relief, as discussed in Church of Christ Charitable Trust v. Ponniamman Educational Trust.

rule.if: later_specific_performance_suit and same_cause_of_action and multiple_reliefs_available and relief_omitted_without_leave

predicates.later_specific_performance_suit: A plaintiff brings a later suit seeking specific performance after an earlier suit concerning the same agreement or transaction.
predicates.same_cause_of_action: The material facts supporting the later claim were also the basis of the earlier suit.
predicates.multiple_reliefs_available: The plaintiff could claim more than one form of relief on the facts supporting the earlier suit.
predicates.relief_omitted_without_leave: The plaintiff omitted the relief later sought and did not obtain the court’s permission to reserve it.

issues.definition: When a plaintiff later seeks a relief available on the same cause of action but omitted it from an earlier suit without permission, the later suit is barred.

issues.legal_issue: The bar on bringing a later suit for an omitted relief applies even when the earlier suit remains pending.
material_facts: The later specific-performance suits were filed while the earlier injunction suits concerning the same properties and agreements were still pending.
The High Court considered itself bound by a decision that confined the bar to cases in which the earlier suit had already been disposed of.
issues.conclusion: The bar applies whether the later suit is filed during the pendency of the earlier suit or after its disposal.
issues.legal_principle: The Court interpreted Order II Rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure in light of its purpose of preventing multiple suits on the same cause of action. It agreed with the approach in Murti v. Bhola Ram and Krishnaji v. Raghunath and rejected the view in R. Vimalchand v. Ramalingam that the earlier suit must first be disposed of.

rule.if: later_suit_for_omitted_relief and first_suit_pending and same_cause_of_action and relief_omitted_without_leave

predicates.later_suit_for_omitted_relief: A plaintiff brings a later suit seeking a relief left out of an earlier suit.
predicates.first_suit_pending: The earlier suit has not been disposed of when the later suit is filed.
predicates.same_cause_of_action: The material facts supporting both suits are the same.
predicates.relief_omitted_without_leave: The plaintiff left the later-sought relief out of the earlier suit without obtaining the court’s permission to reserve it.

issues.definition: The omission bar applies to a later suit on the same cause of action without permission even if the earlier suit is still pending.

issues.legal_issue: A plaintiff need not invariably wait until the stipulated performance date has passed before seeking specific performance when the defendant’s conduct already indicates an intention not to perform.
material_facts: The plaintiff filed the injunction suits before the agreed period for executing the sale deeds had expired.

Before those suits were filed, the defendant had returned the advance payments and communicated concerns about a possible restraint on alienation; the plaintiff alleged that the defendant was seeking to frustrate the agreements and sell the properties to others.
The plaintiff contended that specific performance became actionable only after the agreed period expired and the defendant failed to execute the deeds despite a later legal notice.
issues.conclusion: The expiry of the agreed performance period was not invariably required before the plaintiff could claim specific performance; the earlier pleadings disclosed a basis to include that relief.
issues.legal_principle: Under Vithalbhai (P) Ltd. v. Union Bank of India, prematurity does not go to the root of jurisdiction, and whether a premature suit should be entertained is generally a matter of judicial discretion unless a statute creates a mandatory bar. The Court noted that the Specific Relief Act, 1963 contains no requirement that a plaintiff wait for the performance date to expire where the defendant’s overt acts make the defendant’s intentions clear.

predicates.specific_performance_claim: A plaintiff seeks an order requiring the other party to carry out an agreement to sell property.
predicates.claim_precedes_performance_date: The plaintiff seeks that relief before the time fixed for performance has expired.
predicates.defendant_overt_acts_show_intent_not_to_: The defendant’s conduct communicates an intention not to perform the agreement.

issues.definition: A plaintiff may seek specific performance before the agreed performance date when the defendant’s conduct shows an intention not to perform.
